subject: SS
title: Time Detective Ride
start_sub: True or false? Ride through the right gate.

statements.text: History is the study of the human past.
statements.why: Yes, it looks back at how people lived before us.

statements.text: Geologists study old inscriptions carved on stone.
statements.why: Epigraphists read inscriptions; geologists study Earth's physical features.

statements.text: Palaeontologists learn about life from millions of years ago by studying fossils.
statements.why: Yes, fossils preserve remains of plants, animals and humans.

statements.text: Archaeologists learn about the past by measuring the height of mountains.
statements.why: Archaeologists dig up remains such as tools, pots, beads and bones.

statements.text: A regular Gregorian year has 365 days spread over 12 months.
statements.why: Yes, and a leap year comes every four years.

statements.text: A decade is a period of 100 years.
statements.why: A decade is ten years; a century is 100 years.

statements.text: A millennium is any period of 1,000 years.
statements.why: Yes, and a century is a shorter period of 100 years.

statements.text: BCE years are counted forward from the conventional year of Jesus' birth.
statements.why: BCE years count backward from that point; CE years count forward.

statements.text: Homo sapiens have been on Earth for about 300,000 years.
statements.why: Yes, about three lakh years, a tiny part of Earth's history.

statements.text: Early humans lived mostly as farmers, growing cereals.
statements.why: They were mainly hunters and gatherers; farming came much later.

statements.text: Bands of early humans sometimes swapped beads and tooth pendants with other groups.
statements.why: Yes, they made these from stone, shell and animal teeth.

statements.text: People began using iron first and copper later.
statements.why: Copper came first and iron later.

statements.text: A hamlet is a small settlement or small village.
statements.why: Yes, and over time hamlets grew into larger villages.

statements.text: The last Ice Age ended around 1,000 years ago.
statements.why: It ended around 12,000 years ago.

statements.text: A panchanga is a set of tables with each month's days and sky events.
statements.why: Yes, many people in India still use these tables.

statements.text: A timeline shows the sizes of different countries.
statements.why: A timeline puts dates and events in their order.

statements.text: Compared with Earth's whole story, humans arrived very late and have been here briefly.
statements.why: Yes, Earth's history is far longer than our 300,000 years.

statements.text: Earth's history began about 4.54 million years ago.
statements.why: It began about 4.54 billion years ago.

statements.text: Societies often began a new era from a big event, like a ruler taking charge.
statements.why: Yes, the birth of an important person could mark one too.

statements.text: Scholars can still speak the languages of early humans today.
statements.why: Those early languages are now lost.

statements.text: Hindu, Muslim and Jewish calendars help fix the dates of festivals today.
statements.why: Yes, they are used side by side with the Gregorian calendar.

statements.text: AD marks the years counted after Jesus' death.
statements.why: AD refers to the years after Jesus' birth.

statements.text: The years once marked AD are now called CE.
statements.why: Yes, CE stands for Common Era and is used across the world.

statements.text: The Gregorian calendar has a year zero between 1 BCE and 1 CE.
statements.why: There is no year zero; 1 CE comes straight after 1 BCE.

statements.text: A timeline can use a dotted stretch to skip long periods and save space.
statements.why: Yes, without skipping, long periods would need a huge timeline.

statements.text: Sources of history are limited to written texts.
statements.why: Objects, structures, oral tales and art are sources too.

statements.text: Oral sources such as folklore can help historians learn about the past.
statements.why: Yes, oral sources stand beside archaeological, literary and artistic ones.

statements.text: When two sources disagree, historians must accept both as equally true.
statements.why: Historians choose the source they find more trustworthy.

statements.text: Studying old climates gives historians new clues about the past.
statements.why: Yes, science has helped rebuild the past much more in recent decades.

statements.text: In early farming communities, every person owned a private plot of land.
statements.why: The land was shared; people sowed and harvested it together.

statements.text: The year 1999 falls in the 20th century CE.
statements.why: Yes, the 20th century CE runs from 1901 to 2000.

statements.text: The year 2000 falls in the 21st century CE.
statements.why: The 21st century CE runs from 2001 to 2100.

statements.text: The year 250 BCE falls in the 3rd century BCE.
statements.why: Yes, the 3rd century BCE runs from 300 BCE to 201 BCE.

statements.text: The year 1500 CE falls in the 1st millennium CE.
statements.why: The 2nd millennium CE covers 1001 to 2000, so 1500 belongs there.

statements.text: The year 1600 is a leap year, being a multiple of 400.
statements.why: Yes, century years are leap years when they are multiples of 400.

statements.text: The year 1700 is a leap year in the Gregorian calendar.
statements.why: Century years must be multiples of 400 to be leap years.

statements.text: Between 3 BCE and 3 CE, 5 years pass.
statements.why: Yes: 3 + 3 - 1 = 5, as there is no year zero.

statements.text: Between 5 BCE and 5 CE, exactly 10 years pass.
statements.why: Add and subtract 1: 5 + 5 - 1 = 9 years.

statements.text: A panchanga could help someone find the date of a solar eclipse.
statements.why: Yes, it predicts solar and lunar eclipses precisely.

statements.text: Someone reading an ancient stone inscription is working as a geologist.
statements.why: Epigraphists are the experts who study ancient inscriptions.

statements.text: A person born in 100 BCE was born before someone born in 50 BCE.
statements.why: Yes, BCE years count backward, so the bigger number is earlier.

statements.text: An event in 500 BCE happened after an event in 200 BCE.
statements.why: BCE years count backward, so 500 BCE came before 200 BCE.

statements.text: From 100 BCE to 2000 CE, 2,099 years pass.
From 200 BCE to 100 CE, exactly 300 years pass.
statements.why: With no year zero: 200 + 100 - 1 = 299 years.

statements.text: More food let communities grow, which helped hamlets become villages and then small towns.
statements.why: Yes, and river sites with water and fertile soil made farming easier.

statements.text: The last Ice Age ended before Homo sapiens first appeared.
statements.why: Homo sapiens came 300,000 years ago; that Ice Age ended 12,000 years ago.

statements.text: Even careful historians may end up with gaps, since some pieces of the past stay missing.
statements.why: Yes, like a jigsaw puzzle with some pieces lost.

statements.text: Metal tools appeared before people started settling down and growing cereals.
statements.why: Settling and farming came first; pottery and metal appeared later.
